Q: Missing fields during serialization after upgrading Jackson 2 to Jackson 3 A:

This is a known behavior change in Jackson 3.0, not a bug in your code.

Jackson 3 tightened its accessor-naming rules (see databind#2882) so it no longer auto-detects getX()/setX() methods where the character right after get/set is lowercase or not a letter at all.

In your case, getevents() has a lowercase e immediately after get. Jackson 2 still recognized that as the getter for events, but Jackson 3 doesn't — and it fails silently rather than throwing, which is why the field just vanishes instead of erroring out.

Fix: rename the accessor to follow the standard JavaBean convention:

java
public List<MyEvent> getEvents() { return events; }
public void setEvents(List<MyEvent> events) { this.events = events; }

That's the fix you already found — worth confirming here for anyone else who hits this, since Jackson 3 won't warn you when it silently drops a property this way. If renaming isn't an option (generated code, etc.), Jackson 3 exposes a way to relax this via a custom AccessorNamingStrategy on JsonMapper.Builder — worth checking the current DefaultAccessorNamingStrategy javadoc for the exact builder call, since that part of the API shifted across 3.0 milestones.

Q: Modal close and form value reset not working in Angular A:

Try this.

this.userLoginForm.form.reset()

or

this.userLoginForm.resetForm()

Q: socket_bind() : Only one usage of each socket address (protocol/network address/port) is normally permitted in php A:

In addition to the link @Barmar posted in the comments, I found this article and this one, each of which are pointing to the possibility that you're either running out of ports or using an invalid port number.

I don't have too much experience with Windows in this regards, but that second article at least is claiming that you can either use a port in the range 1024-5000, or change a registry setting if you want to go higher. I would try setting your port to something in that range, say 4950, and see if that clears your issue up.

The registry key in question for any of those interested is HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters\MaxUserPort and the value can go up to 65534. However, I doubt this would be a necessary step, unless you already have ~4000 other processes already running that are using up all of your available ports.

Q: Warning for Connection Abandoned - With tomcat 7 throwing PooledConnection Exception A:

From my research this is related to a stale connection or not closing connections correctly. I have found related ticket here. Please review and let me know if that helps. If not can you provide more information of your environment. Tomcat Fullversion? Looks like your using hibernate. What version? Are there any other errors like maybe in your application logging that could be related?

Q: VBScript error 424 Object Required when running script under SYSTEM account A:

The SYSTEM account has no business connecting to other hosts. Run the script as a user with local admin privileges.

Q: mmap() rejects too small a mapped area A:

An mmap region must be at least one page in length. You can check the source to see.

https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/mm/mmap.c#L336

Remember that what this interface does is create a new virtual mapping for an existing set of pages, so it's always done in units of whole pages.

Q: again Error Code 1054 unknown column in 'field list' error on MySQL without Group Concat Actor A:

sakila.actor is a table, not a column.

sakila.actor.first_name is a column.

You probably want:

concat(`sakila`.`actor`.`first_name`, _utf8mb4' ', `sakila`.`actor`.`last_name`)   AS `actor`

You'll also need to change the grouping, to give one row per film per category per actor, with...

GROUP BY
   `sakila`.`film`.`film_id`, 
   `sakila`.`category`.`name`,
   `sakila`.`actor`.`actor_id`

Q: Power BI Identical Measures Giving Different Results A:

The difference is caused by data lineage.

DISTINCT(ALL(Fact[Upper])) keeps the lineage of the original column. When SUMX iterates over it, the implicit CALCULATE inside [Sum_Prod] converts the row context into a filter context that filters the model to the current row's value.

Functions like ROW and UNION break lineage. Because that manually built table has no connection to your model, context transition doesn't happen. Inside Upper_Wrong, [Sum_Prod] evaluates without being filtered by the current row. In your visual, the outer filter context already restricts Fact[Upper] to the current row, so [Sum_Prod] returns that row's total; the SUMX then sums that same value three times, resulting in 3 * [Sum_Prod] per row.

To use a manual list while keeping the correct behavior, use TREATAS to map the lineage back to the column:

Upper_Wrong_Fixed =
VAR myGroup =
    UNION(
        ROW("Upper", "A"),
        ROW("Upper", "B"),
        ROW("Upper", "C")
    )
VAR myGroupWithLineage = TREATAS( myGroup, Fact[Upper] )
RETURN
    SUMX(
        myGroupWithLineage,
        [Sum_Prod]
    )

This forces the context transition to filter Fact[Upper] as it iterates. For a deeper look at why this happens, see Understanding data lineage in DAX.
